newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seguin, Monory disagree on BoF nominees - sources.
newsitem.headline: Seguin, Monory disagree on BoF nominees - sources.

text.p: French National Assembly president Philippe Seguin, Senate president Rene Monory, and Economic and Social Council (CES) head Jean Matteoli have failed to agree a list of nominees for the Bank of France monetary policy council and will submit separate lists, sources close to the process said on Tuesday.

The sources said the main disagreement was between Monory, an ardent pro-European, and Seguin, who campaigned against the Maastricht treaty in a 1992 referendum before relucantly falling into line over EMU and who also favours a weaker franc and faster interest rate cuts.

The government has to decide before the end of the year whether to replace or reinstate two members of the nine-member council - journalist Jean Boissonnat and banker Bruno de Maulde - because their mandates expire on January 6. Neither has given any indication they want to step down.
The possible replacement of the two has unnerved financial markets, on fears the government might use it as an excuse to try and soften the Bank's policy on interest rates.
The Bank has been very cautious in lowering rates in order to keep the franc stable against other core currencies in the European exchange rate mechanism.

Seguin put forward Robert Pelletier, a member of the CES, formerly managing director of the association of credit establishments (Afec) and Alain Prate, a member of the CES, a treasury offical and an ex-deputy governor of the central bank.
Matteoli put forward Pierre Guillen, ex-head of the CNPF employers federation and Jean-Rene Bernard, formerly head of regional bank CIC and deputy governor of Credit Foncier.
However, the sources said Seguin had in fact persuaded Matteoli to put foward Guillen, a well known opponent of the government's so-called "franc fort" policy.
"Guillen is Seguin's candidate. He convinced Matteoli," the sources said.
Monory proposed to reinstate Boissonnat and to replace de Maulde with Pierre Achard an aide to former Prime Minister Raymond Barre and now senior economic advisor with the French embassy in Germany.
Seguin's official candidates may have a lesser chance of being selected because Boissonnat and de Maulde were initially nominated by the presidents of the Senate and the CES.

Under French law the cabinet can choose the two nominees either from a joint list of six names submitted by the three parties, or in the case of disagreement, from three separate lists each containing two names.
However, standard practice suggests that the potential replacements could well be chosen from the lists forwarded by the institutions who nominated the encumbents in question.
The Bank's monetary policy council expresses an opinion which is passed on to the government for a final decision.
The government declined to comment on the individual nominees.

"What we want is for interest rates to continue to come down and that the Bank of France's monetary policy doesn't obstruct government policy. And it doesn't at the moment," a source at the Prime Minister's office said.
